agent_position: Two fixed triggers: a lease entering release_failed for any reason, and a teardown attempt failing with an operator-repairable class while a retry is scheduled
owner_disposition: Operator events are a general operator-relevant state change, an open set of kinds that a new producer extends with little patching; operators may want events even for successful long-running jobs, not only held work
summary: Operator events become a general, extensible kind set rather than two held-work triggers

agent_position: A foundation kit for operator events (declared kinds, recorder in the caller's transaction, its own store and drain to sinks), beside the existing per-event outboxes
owner_disposition: A foundation kit, reused by registries, storefronts, provisioning and non-compute domains (API credits, inference, compute jobs); and one singular eventing system that replaces the lease-ended events, with each outbox a consumer of it rather than event handling added one type at a time
summary: The event kit becomes the one eventing system; existing lease-ended events and outboxes become its consumers

agent_position: E4: a rich envelope of our own whose routing fields are first-class, mapped onto CloudEvents 1.0 with a CloudEvents rendering at the webhook sink
owner_disposition: E2: the rich envelope alone; a CloudEvents mapping and rendering waits until there is a definite receiver for it
summary: Envelope is E2; the CloudEvents rendering is deferred until a definite receiver exists

agent_position: S2: build the event kit with the full consumer model here and give the move of the lease-end events, the signed-report outbox and the capacity-release outbox to replace-polling-with-authenticated-push (S2b, a follow-up change, if push is not near)
owner_disposition: S1: this change builds the kit and moves all three onto it; push is not coming soon, work focuses on finishing roadmap goals 1 and 8, and the other changes sharing this work are updated during this change
summary: This change moves the lease-end events and both provisioning outboxes onto the event kit itself

agent_position: R3: routes by kind pattern and severity plus our own declarative predicates (eq, in, gte, lte, exists) over declared attributes and related references
owner_disposition: R3's intent, but no query language of our own: a route is a select+where, evaluated by an adopted open-source library executing SQL over the JSON-renderable envelope; if no good package exists, fall back to R2
summary: Route predicates come from an adopted SQL-over-objects library, else routing is kind and severity only

agent_position: T2: retention declared per kind (always, or days), lengthened but not shortened by configuration, pruned only once every consumer has passed
owner_disposition: Retention by time, configurable per table, as the repository's standing practice; retention by severity or kind is deferred; the aim is bounded state growth and extensibility
summary: Event retention is time-based and configured per table, not declared per kind

agent_position: F2: per-consumer retry policy; an operator sink retries to a maximum age, then marks the delivery abandoned, visible on a status read
owner_disposition: F3: an abandoned delivery goes to a finally sink, defaulting to the log
summary: Abandoned deliveries go to a configurable finally sink that defaults to the log

agent_position: partly: the resume promise and the pruning rule conflict; recommended (A), a parked or pending destination holds the prune gate until it moves on, with a destination retired when its peer leaves the configuration
owner_disposition: Accept the risk that parked destinations can lose events: a parked destination counts as passed for pruning and resume delivers only what is retained; a destination whose peer is no longer configured counts as passed the same way, its undelivered events going to the finally sink when it is retired
summary: Parked destinations do not hold back pruning; the owner accepts losing events pruned during a long park
